strings.d1.s0.name: Fisherman's Bastion
strings.d1.s0.tips: Fairytale turrets and a view over Parliament. The lower terraces are free; the upper tower costs 1,500 HUF (free before 08:00).
strings.d1.s1.name: Matthias Church
strings.d1.s1.tips: Colourful Zsolnay-tiled roof; a coronation church with a mosaic interior.
strings.d1.s2.name: Buda Castle & Castle Hill Yürüyüşü
strings.d1.s2.tips: Palace courtyards and the Turul bird statue. The Hungarian National Gallery (4,400 HUF) is optional.
strings.d1.s3.name: Ruszwurm Cukrászda
strings.d1.s3.tips: The oldest pastry shop, open since 1827; try the krémes (cream-filled puff pastry). It has 5 tables. Afterwards take the funicular and walk across the Chain Bridge to Pest.
strings.d1.s4.name: Gerlóczy Kávéház
strings.d1.s4.tips: A Parisian-style café in Belváros; goulash and paprikás.
strings.d1.b0.name: Halászbástya Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: Set inside Fisherman's Bastion with views; expensive.
strings.d1.b1.name: Hospital in the Rock
strings.d1.b1.tips: A WWII hospital and nuclear bunker beneath the castle; a guided tour is compulsory.
strings.d2.s0.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
strings.d2.s0.tips: 45-minute tour (Holy Crown). Book online days in advance and bring your passport.
strings.d2.s1.name: St. Stephen's Basilica
strings.d2.s1.tips: Holds the mummified right hand of St Stephen; the dome panorama costs 3,000 HUF.
strings.d2.s2.name: Belvárosi Disznótoros
strings.d2.s2.tips: Hungarian butcher's food sold by weight: hurka (liver sausage), kolbász (sausage), eaten standing up.
strings.d2.s3.name: Heroes' Square
strings.d2.s3.tips: Take Metro line 1 (the oldest metro on the continent). See the Millennium Monument and the seven tribal chieftains.
strings.d2.s4.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
strings.d2.s4.tips: Europe's largest thermal bath: a yellow palace, a 38°C outdoor pool and people playing chess. Bring your own slippers and towel; cheaper on weekdays.
strings.d2.b0.name: Gellért Thermal Bath
strings.d2.b0.tips: An Art Nouveau bath; an alternative to Széchenyi.
strings.d2.b1.name: Vajdahunyad Vár Restoranı Városliget
strings.d2.b1.tips: A restaurant in the castle park.
strings.d3.s0.name: Dohány Street Synagogue
strings.d3.s0.tips: Europe's largest synagogue, with the Weeping Willow memorial. Closed on Saturdays.
strings.d3.s1.name: Karaván Street Food
strings.d3.s1.tips: A food-truck courtyard next to Szimpla; try lángos (fried dough with garlic and cheese) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake).
strings.d3.s2.name: Great Market Hall
strings.d3.s2.tips: An iron market hall from 1897: paprika, salami and lángos upstairs. Closed on Sundays.
strings.d3.s3.name: Liberty Bridge & Gellért Hill
strings.d3.s3.tips: The green bridge, then a 30-minute climb up Gellért Hill. At sunset, enjoy the panorama from the Citadella.
strings.d3.s4.name: Szimpla Kert
strings.d3.s4.tips: Open in winter too; farmers' market on Sunday mornings.
strings.d3.b0.name: Mazel Tov
strings.d3.b0.tips: A Middle Eastern garden restaurant in the Jewish Quarter; book ahead.
strings.d3.b1.name: Hungarian National Museum
strings.d3.b1.tips: The steps associated with the 1848 revolution; an alternative to the market.
strings.d4.s0.name: Szentendre Fő tér
strings.d4.s0.tips: 40 minutes by HÉV train (from Batthyány tér); a Baroque artists' town with Serbian churches.
strings.d4.s1.name: Blagoveštenska Church Szentendre
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Serbian Orthodox church on the square.
strings.d4.s2.name: Aranysárkány Vendéglő
strings.d4.s2.tips: The town's classic restaurant; goulash and chicken paprikás.
strings.d4.s3.name: Szentendre Danube Embankment
strings.d4.s3.tips: A riverside walk in winter; take the HÉV back.
strings.d4.s4.name: Skanzen Open Air Museum
strings.d4.s4.tips: Skanzen has limited opening in winter; visit the town's galleries and the Margit Kovács Museum instead.
strings.d4.b0.name: Álom Lángos Szentendre
strings.d4.b0.tips: The town's famous lángos; a small stand.
strings.d4.b1.name: Visegrád Castle
strings.d4.b1.tips: A castle on the Danube Bend; go by bus, instead of Skanzen.
strings.d5.s0.name: Margaret Island
strings.d5.s0.tips: A park island in the Danube; rent a bike or a pedal cart, and see the musical fountain, the Japanese garden and the ruins.
strings.d5.s1.name: Andrássy Avenue
strings.d5.s1.tips: A UNESCO-listed boulevard with the Opera, Liszt Square and luxury shops.
strings.d5.s2.name: Menza Liszt Ferenc tér
strings.d5.s2.tips: A retro Hungarian restaurant on Liszt Square; try the goulash.
strings.d5.s3.name: House of Terror
strings.d5.s3.tips: The former Nazi and communist secret police headquarters; harrowing but important. Closed on Mondays.
strings.d5.s4.name: Hungarian State Opera
strings.d5.s4.tips: A tour of the Neo-Renaissance opera house (in English at 13:30 and 15:00), or evening tickets from 5,000 HUF.
strings.d5.b0.name: New York Café
strings.d5.b0.tips: Billed as the world's most beautiful café; expect a queue and high prices. An alternative to Menza.
strings.d5.b1.name: Miniversum
strings.d5.b1.tips: Miniature Hungarian railways; an alternative to the House of Terror (with children).
strings.d6.s0.name: Aquincum Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: Ruins of a Roman city; take the HÉV to Óbuda.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lukács Thermal Bath
strings.d6.s1.tips: The locals' bath; quieter and cheaper than Széchenyi.
strings.d6.s2.name: Bambi Eszpresszó
strings.d6.s2.tips: A communist-era café unchanged since 1961; in Buda.
strings.d6.s3.name: Batthyány tér Parliament View
strings.d6.s3.tips: The best view of Parliament, framed from across the river.
strings.d6.s4.name: Danube Sightseeing Cruise
strings.d6.s4.tips: A 1-hour daytime boat ride; glass-covered in winter, with illuminated views after 17:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Pesti Disznó
strings.d6.b0.tips: Modern Hungarian cooking centred on pork; in Pest.
strings.d6.b1.name: Óbuda Fő tér
strings.d6.b1.tips: The old Óbuda square with its statues holding umbrellas; an alternative to Aquincum.
strings.d7.s0.name: Váci Street
strings.d7.s0.tips: A pedestrian shopping street; buy paprika and Tokaji wine as souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Vörösmarty Square Gerbeaud
strings.d7.s1.tips: A pastry shop dating from 1858; have Dobos torta and coffee as a farewell.
strings.d7.s2.name: Danube Promenade Little Princess
strings.d7.s2.tips: The Little Princess statue and tram line 2 running along the river.
strings.d7.s3.name: Deák Ferenc tér 100E Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: The direct 100E bus takes 40 minutes; farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Café Central Budapest
strings.d7.b0.tips: A literary café from 1887; an alternative to Gerbeaud.
strings.d7.b1.name: Erzsébet tér Ferris Wheel
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Budapest Eye Ferris wheel; an alternative to the river.
strings.note0: A Budapest Card or 24-hour ticket costs about 2,500 HUF; tram line 2 has views of the riverbank. The 100E airport bus costs 2,200 HUF. Metro line 1 is historic.
strings.note1: Winter temperatures range from -2 to 5°C; the Vörösmarty Christmas market runs November to December. Baths with steaming outdoor pools are best in the snow! Széchenyi holds a Saturday 'sparty'.
strings.note2: Baths cost 12,000-15,000 HUF (cheaper on weekdays), Parliament 10,000 and the synagogue 12,000. Renting a towel and slippers is expensive, so bring your own.
strings.note3: Goulash (it's a soup!), pörkölt (meat stew), lángos, kürtőskalács, Dobos torta. Tip 10-12%; check whether a 'szervizdíj' (service charge) has already been added to the bill.
strings.note4: Get forints in cash. Places that accept EUR give a poor exchange rate. Beware the 'no commission' trap at currency exchange offices. At ATMs, choose your own bank's rate.
strings.note5: The ruin bars are around Kazinczy Street; the synagogue is closed on Saturdays and the Great Market Hall on Sundays.
